findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the quarantine seam doctor will reuse (e.g. promote/expose rebar._store.sync._quarantine_untracked) and add sync.py to Scope, or specify the shared helper doctor calls so the quarantine-path logic is not duplicated.
evidence: Plan: 'move class-2 paths into the quarantine directory established by change 1757 (<git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/ — move, never delete)'
sync.py:248 defines `_quarantine_untracked` (leading underscore = private) as the only producer of that path; sync.py:260 builds `common_dir.resolve() / 'reconverge-quarantine' / stamp`
Scope lists fsck_tracker_health.py and doctor.py but no sync.py edit/export
findings.finding: The plan says doctor should 'move class-2 paths into the quarantine directory established by change 1757', but the mechanism that creates reconverge-quarantine/<ts>/ is the PRIVATE helper _quarantine_untracked in src/rebar/_store/sync.py — a consumer outside doctor.py's directory that the plan neither names nor enumerates as reused/refactored. The Scope section lists no edit or export of sync.py.
scenarios: Implementer must either duplicate the quarantine path/move logic in doctor.py or promote _quarantine_untracked to a shared seam; the plan specifies neither.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the lock phasing so the class-1 `git checkout`/class-2 move actions run under a single explicit write_lock hold, but the post-repair reconverge (which acquires the write lock itself, and whose sibling event-writes are non-reentrant) runs AFTER that hold is released — and reconcile AC-3's 'entirely under the store write lock' with reconverge's self-locking.
evidence: Plan: 'repair actions that run under the store write lock (rebar._store.lock.write_lock)' ... 'invoke the existing reconverge entry (rebar._store.sync.reconverge) so a previously wedged store converges in the same command'
doctor.py run_repair lines 234-242: 'NO outer write lock. ... that lock is NOT re-entrant: an outer hold made each inner acquisition block until its 60s timeout and fail'
sync.py:328 reconverge acquires 'with _lock.write_lock(tracker, timeout=lock_timeout, attempts=1, dual_window=True)' and on LockTimeout skips the round
AC line 3: 'Repair runs entirely under the store write lock' — contradicted by the reconverge phase which must self-lock
findings.finding: The plan says repair runs 'under the store write lock' and then 'invoke the existing reconverge entry' — but doctor's existing run_repair deliberately holds NO outer write lock because the lock is non-reentrant (event writes self-lock), and reconverge() acquires the write lock internally. Wrapping the repair actions and the reconverge call in one outer write_lock hold would make reconverge's own acquisition time out and silently skip, so the store would not converge.
findings.location: Approach — Repair paragraph; Acceptance Criteria line 3
scenarios: doctor --repair on a wedged store: class-1/2 healed but reconverge's inner write_lock acquisition times out under the outer hold, store stays diverged, AC-2 fails
findings.suggested_fix: Hold write_lock only around the raw checkout/move steps (which do not self-lock); release it before calling reconverge(), which re-acquires the lock internally. Reword AC-3 to 'the file-mutating repair steps run under the write lock; reconverge self-locks after release'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the write-lock design: state how the new class-1/class-2 file repairs acquire the write lock without re-entrant deadlock against run_repair's documented 'NO outer write lock' rule and the reconverge() call that takes its own lock.
evidence: Plan: 'repair actions that run under the store write lock (rebar._store.lock.write_lock)'

doctor.py:234-242 run_repair docstring: 'NO outer write lock. Every event write already takes the tracker write lock for itself ... and that lock is NOT re-entrant: an outer hold made each inner acquisition block until its 60s timeout and fail'
The reconverge() post-repair call itself acquires the write lock (sync.py:272-273), so wrapping it inside another held write lock risks the same non-reentrant deadlock.
findings.finding: The plan extends doctor.py's existing run_repair registry to run new repairs 'under the store write lock', but the existing run_repair deliberately takes NO outer write lock (its docstring warns the write lock is non-reentrant and an outer hold deadlocks the per-event acquisitions). The new class-1/class-2 actions are raw git/filesystem operations rather than event writes, so lock discipline is a real integration decision the plan glosses over by claiming the registry already provides it.
findings.location: Approach / Repair; AC line 3 ('Repair runs entirely under the store write lock')
scenarios: Implementer wraps the new file-repair loop AND the reconverge call in an outer write_lock, reproducing the deadlock the existing code was written to avoid.
